children: China retains a substantial cost and execution advantage in data-center construction, Creditsights analysts say in a research note. Data-center development costs in Southeast Asia are 25%-30% higher than in China, which has a mature supply chain, established contractor ecosystem and relatively low operating costs, they note. It takes around six to nine months to build a data center in China, compared with 12-15 months in Southeast Asia and even longer in Europe and the U.S., they say. In Southeast Asia, Malaysia is relatively well positioned for further data-center development given its proximity to Singapore and comparatively well-developed infrastructure, they add. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
